decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right; begin a continuous elbow-up right-arm side-grasp approach, leaving the left arm for pens.
Advance right gripper toward the holder from its right side while leveling the grasp; keep clear of the rim.
Align the open right jaws around the holder body, using the head-view estimate of its center.
Correct for the holder's small displacement, then close the right gripper around its sides; retention still needs a lift check.
The holder is not retained and shifted ahead of the jaws. Reopen, back away laterally, and align before a straight side approach.
Approach the holder along the right gripper's forward axis with jaws open, avoiding sideways contact.
Back off from the contacted holder and correct depth alignment; reassess its upright state before closing.
Holder has fallen onto its side. Approach its body from above with the right gripper, to lift and turn it upright.
The rotation was rejected without motion. Retract and lift at fixed orientation to regain configuration margin before reorienting.
Use much smaller pitch increments while retracting to avoid the previous IK discontinuity.
Reduce pitch increments and introduce yaw while retracting, moving away from the wrist singularity without changing elbow branch.
Pitch toward a top-down recovery grasp while moving above the fallen holder, keeping the right elbow-up branch continuous.
Continue above the holder's right end and finish the downward gripper orientation with small continuous increments.
Lower to regain reach margin and slow the orientation change after the continuity interruption.
Move toward the fallen holder's right end at fixed attitude, keeping the wrist on the right side of the workspace.
The forward target exceeded the current IK margin. Retract and ease toward a side-oriented recovery grasp rather than forcing the folded configuration.
Level the right gripper for an axial side grasp of the fallen holder, with gradual lowering and configuration continuity.
Finish leveling while aligning farther forward with the fallen holder; keep an axial clearance before advancing the jaws.
Wrist view still shows the holder off-center along depth. Shift forward with lateral clearance, then reassess before closing.
Back out of the reach limit and angle the right gripper toward the holder so its fingers can reach without further forward wrist extension.
Advance the open jaws around the fallen holder's near end, then close for a lift-and-right recovery test.
Keep the right gripper closed and lift/retract gently to check whether the holder is retained.
The holder remained on the table. Reopen and lower the jaws toward its body rather than its upper surface, with a small forward correction.
Bring the open jaws down to the fallen holder's mid-height, angling forward to avoid further wrist extension.
The low target contacted the table. Raise slightly and shift the jaw center back across the holder body, correcting the depth estimate.
Close on the holder's near end and perform a short vertical retention test.
The holder is still outside the jaw center in the wrist view. Reopen and correct laterally across the gripper axis while returning to body height.
The holder is now centered between the open jaws in the wrist image. Close and make a short lift to verify retention.
The jaws closed before reaching around the holder end. Reopen and insert farther along the holder while lowering slightly, keeping the wrist on the right.
Close at the deeper body alignment, then lift and retract slightly to verify retention in the images.
Lower the open jaws to the holder's side midline and level them; the previous closure appears to have passed above its body.
The low motion contacted the table. Lift off and realign the gripper axially with the holder, reducing the oblique approach and depth error.
Use the wrist view to shift the open jaw center toward the holder while preserving a little forward gripper angle and wrist reach margin.
The holder body is centered between the jaws. Close and lift while retracting from the reach limit; verify that the holder moves with the hand.
The holder remains unretained. Advance the open jaws substantially farther over its near end at body height, keeping the wrist right of the midline.
Correct the remaining wrist-view lateral offset by angling the jaws forward, then close without lifting so contact can be inspected.
Hold the close target to let the jaws finish closing, then lift gently while retracting to check retention.
Repeated right-side grasps have not retained the holder. Withdraw the right arm and start a left-side recovery approach within the left workspace.
Clear the right arm and bring the left gripper forward above the pens toward the holder's open end.
Advance the left arm above the table toward the holder, keeping both arms separated and the open jaws clear of the pens.
Move the left open gripper forward and gradually down toward the holder's open end, using a side approach with clearance.
Center the fallen holder in the left wrist view by correcting depth and lowering to its side midline; right arm stays clear.
Shift the left jaws toward the remaining lateral offset and deeper around the holder rim, then close without lifting for inspection.
Allow the left closure to finish, then perform a small lift/retraction to test whether the holder follows.
The left grasp missed. Correct the depth estimate toward the near side of the holder and lower the open jaws to its center height before another closure.
Switch to an angled overhead recovery grasp: lift and retract the left hand before changing pitch, avoiding more table-level side contacts.
Tilt the left gripper downward while lifting and retracting, preserving elbow-up continuity for an angled grasp of the fallen holder.
Bring the angled left gripper over the fallen holder and increase downward pitch gradually; the right hand remains clear.
Shift the left angled grasp forward toward the holder rather than the adjacent pen, using small fixed-attitude increments.
Close the left jaws at the current holder contact and pause to inspect whether they surround its body before lifting.
The closure was short of the holder. Reopen, flatten the approach slightly, and advance the fingertips into the body region without forcing the wrist farther forward.
Rotate the left jaw opening across the holder's short dimension rather than along its length, with a small clearance lift first.
Finish aligning the jaws across the holder's short axis and advance gently along the gripper approach direction.
Close the left jaws across the holder body and allow closure to settle before attempting a lift.
Keep the left gripper closed and lift/retract slowly to determine whether the holder is retained.
The holder did not lift. Reopen and lower at the current depth rather than advancing farther, while reducing roll to put the jaw opening across its sides.
Correct the holder's leftward offset in the wrist image with a small forward shift at fixed gripper attitude before closing again.
Close on the centered holder body, pause for jaw travel, then make a small lift to check retention visually.
The jaws again closed above the holder. Reopen and lower vertically to place the fingertips beside its body, without advancing farther.
At the lower grasp height, recenter the holder between the jaws with a small forward shift, then close without lifting.
Let the left closure settle, then lift and retract a few centimeters with the gripper closed to test retention.
The fingers still close short of the holder. Reopen and advance along the gripper axis rather than only changing height, checking reach continuity.
Replan after the IK limit: retract slightly and turn the angled grasp to run along the holder's length, aligning the jaw opening horizontally across its width.
The orientation change was rejected without motion. Retract at fixed attitude first to restore joint margin.
Reduce the initial retreat to millimeter steps to satisfy the joint-continuity guard, then gradually increase once away from the limit.
With more joint margin, align the left gripper along the holder's length and level its jaw opening across the short dimension.
Replan after the rotation limit: shift the left wrist outward and slightly back at fixed attitude to restore joint margin and center the holder under the jaws.
Use a shallower angled approach while moving forward and down, centering the holder and avoiding the previous wrist reach limit.
Turn the left gripper toward the holder visible off the left edge of its wrist view, rather than extending the wrist farther forward.
Make a final small yaw correction toward the holder and close the left jaws at fixed position, allowing time for closure.
Reopen and advance farther along the left gripper axis so the holder reaches the inner jaw surfaces rather than only the tips; inspect before lifting.
Allow the left jaws to finish closing at the deeper contact, then lift a short distance with the close target held to check retention.
Reopen and roll the jaws across the holder's narrow dimension while returning to the lower contact height; the holder was not retained.
Close across the holder's now-aligned narrow sides and allow the jaw motion to settle before a retention test.
Test the closed contact with a gentle lift and retraction, beginning a small righting rotation only if the holder follows.
The lift confirms another miss above the holder. Reopen and bring the fingertips substantially lower and forward toward the body, with fixed attitude.
Clear the tabletop and remove excessive gripper roll so the jaws open more horizontally rather than one finger contacting the table.
Approach farther forward with a shallower, level-jaw attitude to reach the holder body rather than closing short of it.
The holder is centered but its length exceeds the jaw opening. Roll the gripper to close across its short dimension, with a small clearance lift.
Lower the rolled jaw center to the holder's mid-height, then close across its short dimension without lifting yet.
